To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the set of all valid object histories for one type of object is closed under the application of interval queries, and that the set of valid object histories for another type of object is the result of applying interval queries to the valid object histories of a third type of object.
the closure property holds if and only if the CSSs satisfy a certain condition, called ‘interval query closure condition’.
the set of all interval queries on object histories described by a given CSS has a CSS as its closure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
interval queries on object histories.
the question of how the closure properties of interval queries can be used for a more compact representation of the object histories.
the mathematical foundation for the study of interval queries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given CSS, the set of all CSS’s for which the corresponding interval query is closed is a set which is not empty, but not finitely generated.
interval queries are a powerful and useful tool for analyzing historical data for objects.
the set of all interval queries is closed under intersection, union and complement, and under the operation which returns the set of all histories which are subhistories of a given history.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a mathematical foundation for interval queries on object histories, and we have shown that this foundation is useful for developing efficient query evaluation techniques.
interval queries are not closed under the operation of ‘union of CSS’ (which is a natural operation in the model).
we provide a mathematical framework for describing object histories, and we show a closure property of the interval queries on object histories described by CSS’s.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interval queries can be used to express a wide range of interesting queries on object histories.
interval queries can be applied to object histories in a way that preserves the closure property of the original CSS.
, by using a suitable CSS, we can describe the set of all histories which satisfy a given interval query.
